name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah was a male Levite known for his role in the sacred musical ministry of ancient Israel. As the son of Heman, he was set apart to prophesy through music using lyres, harps, and cymbals, demonstrating a special calling within the tribe of Levi. He was notably chosen ninth by lot among the singers, highlighting his recognized position in the worship leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a divine bestowal or blessing associated with his identity. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:4, emphasizes his connection to God's provision and purpose.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mattaniah as the son of Heman, situating him within a prominent Levitical family known for their musical and prophetic service. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah's significance lies in his dedicated service as one of the appointed singers chosen by lot to prophesy musically, a ministry that combined worship and divine inspiration. His role as the ninth chosen singer underlines the ordered and God-ordained structure of Levitical worship in Israel. Through his lineage and function, Mattaniah contributed to the spiritual life of Israel by facilitating prophetic expression through music.
